{"content":"1|# Local release activation
2|
3|The current native release controller prepares golden, transfers a read-only
4|snapshot with `btrfs send/receive`, and rotates read-only overlays directly at
5|the inventory's owned host targets. It retains active and previous slots.
6|The older per-file/current-symlink procedures below are historical, not an
7|alternative activation path.
8|
9|## Paths and ownership
10|
11|| Path | Purpose |
12||---|---|
13|| `/opt/op-dbus/golden` | Writable preparation subvolume; never an execution target |
14|| `/opt/op-dbus/release-send/<release-id>` | Immutable source generation used by the native transfer |
15|| Native filesystem roots `@release-a` / `@release-b` | Controller-owned received slots; never populate or select manually |
16|| Inventory-declared host targets | Read-only overlays selected by the activation transaction |
17|| `/var/lib/opdbus-release` | Protected controller state, transaction recovery and first-activation preservation |
18|
19|Retention is configurable per storage owner; there is no global five-subvolume
20|cap. Budget free bytes for preparation, send/receive and a recovery reserve
21|before starting writes. Count paths under the release root explicitly: `btrfs
22|subvolume list -o` on an ordinary directory lists descendants of its
23|containing subvolume, including unrelated Incus storage. Existing unrelated
24|subvolumes are not permission to delete storage. Preserve the category,
25|timing, vector and state subvolumes owned by cache/Snowball. Retain the previous active
26|release for rollback; retire only explicitly identified obsolete releases.
27|
28|## Current entry point and base prerequisites
29|
30|Run `sudo ./activate-golden.sh` from the repository root, preserving the
31|explicit prepared-artifact selectors described below. It validates the
32|independent root-owned release kit, provisions/reconciles slots, prepares
33|golden, then invokes native release/activation. It does not compile or reseal.
34|Use `/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch status` for the
35|authoritative slot, journal, overlay and readiness receipt; `rollback` selects
36|the compatible previous release through the same controller.
37|
38|Independent base prerequisites must be ready before the application cutover:
39|
40|- `identity-roots` restores only existing identity-root inventory. An empty
41|  inventory succeeds without provisioning; any failed restoration fails the
42|  service. Login/start/stop never add or remove Btrfs members. Its readiness
43|  marker is emitted only after successful restoration.
44|- On the restored host, the native Open vSwitch package owns its daemons.
45|  The runit `ovsdb-server` service observes the validated native PID with
46|  procps `pidwait`; its bounded check queries the actual Unix socket for
47|  `Open_vSwitch`. It must not launch duplicate daemons, change topology, or
48|  run the old uplink/bootstrap chain. Inspect sockets with native metadata
49|  and protocol tools; a generic directory listing can omit them.
50|- Independent `op-warp-endpoint` restores only the existing declared local
51|  endpoint from `/etc/op-dbus/warp-ssh.json`; `endpoint.sh check` verifies
52|  ownership, address/peer, aliases and MTU. An UP persistent TUN with
53|  NO-CARRIER is not evidence of SSH, remote ingress or authenticated access.
54|  This service does not restore MASQUE, firewall or policy-routing state.
55|- Logger definitions require the existing system `svlog` account/group and
56|  appropriately owned log directories. Long-lived helper services use the
57|  available `sleep infinity`, not an assumed `pause` executable.
58|
59|Runtime TLS, protected capability/toolset policy, provider keys and the
60|production router's matching configuration/token state remain outside the
61|release. The runtime MCP audience and toolset JSON files must be root-owned
62|mode 0600; the bridge rejects group/world-readable policy before binding.
63|Restore missing inputs only from a verified authoritative backup,
64|without printing secret values, overwriting present state, substituting
65|template grants or minting replacement identities. A router token must match
66|the same production gateway's persisted token hash; an unrelated historical
67|configuration is not recovery proof.
68|
69|On this host, `op-storage` and `op-storage-kernel-guard` remain persistently
70|OFF until explicit owner reauthorization. Activation is not permission to
71|rearm them. Enable the independent early-boot release hook only after a
72|successful activation receipt; do not reboot as a deployment check. A
73|received inactive slot is not a deployed application or a mounted 3tchedFS.
74|
75|
76|## Prepare
77|
78|Build the native glibc workspace, prepare its pinned UI and threetched
79|artifacts, and explicitly seal/persist with the freshly built `opblob` and
80|the service's schema-shaping environment. Preserve the previous catalogs and
81|review additions/removals before a live reseal. `build-golden.sh` accepts
82|`OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE` for isolated release preparation.
83|
84|Reuse already-built native binaries by setting `OP_RELEASE_DIR` to the complete
85|prepared executable directory; the default is `target/release`. Set
86|`EMQX_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR` and `MCP_PROVIDER_ARTIFACT_CACHE_DIR` when the pinned
87|EMQX archive and nlm wheel are cached outside `/var/cache/op-dbus/source-artifacts`.
88|These selectors do not rebuild binaries or weaken artifact digest checks.
89|The pinned EMQX archive is still digest-verified before extraction. Its unused
90|esockd demonstration private key is excluded from the prepared payload;
91|configured runtime TLS keys remain outside the release at `/etc/emqx/certs`.
92|
93|The execution payload requires GNU Python 3.14. When the host default differs,
94|`OP_EXECUTION_PYTHON_BUNDLE` may name an existing standalone native runtime
95|directory. Preparation copies that runtime into the execution payload, verifies
96|its relocated base prefix, and installs the hash-locked tools into that private
97|prefix. The received release therefore does not depend on a user-managed
98|interpreter under `/home`; the host's default Python is unchanged. Without this
99|selector, preparation retains the native-host virtual-environment path.
100|The preparation receipt records the runtime binary and preparer digests, so a
101|changed interpreter or preparation implementation invalidates reuse.
102|
103|Golden preparation generates the restart inventory from the prepared bytes.
104|Shell assignments are not executable names; quoted substitutions, continuations,
105|declared function arguments and attached redirection paths retain their
106|dependencies without executing the scripts. Captured-source and versioned
107|skill-packaging provenance are classified by their complete JSON structure,
108|not by filename. Unknown executable/configuration references, mixed provenance
109|and configuration records, and absent release inputs still stop preparation.
110|An inventory-helper repair can be built and selected independently; it does
111|not require replacing the existing application binaries or their catalog.
112|
113|When a plugin version changes, rebuild `op-grpc-bridge` from the same plugin
114|source as `opblob` and activate that bridge with the matching catalog. The
115|bridge compares each sealed plugin version and method declaration with its
116|compiled compatibility contract before dispatch. Building only the sealer,
117|even for a description-only version change, leaves the old bridge rejecting
118|calls. Catalog parity and bridge readiness alone do not verify this boundary.
119|
120|Before the workspace build and sealing, select the prepared threetched binary
121|with the paired absolute `THREETCHED_CAPTURE_BIN` and
122|`THREETCHED_CAPTURE_MANIFEST` paths. Keep those selectors identical across both
123|steps; without them discovery uses the installed binary, which may belong to
124|the previous release. The runtime selectors remain `/usr/bin/threetched` and
125|`/usr/share/op-dbus/threetched-manifests/tched-router.json`. Follow the
126|[binary feature preparation procedure](../../../crates/threetched-fs/README.md#add-a-threetched-feature-from-the-binary)
127|for the exact environment, isolated `opblob seal-plugins` invocation, catalog
128|review and mounted verification. Golden preparation rejects mismatched sealed
129|binary or manifest digests.
130|
131|### Provisioning helper payload and ownership
132|
133|Golden includes the provisioning suite in the existing `libexec/3tched`
134|prepared directory. The inventory maps that directory to the read-only host
135|target **`/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers`**, not the base-system
136|`/usr/local/libexec/3tched` directory. Invoke the activated entry point as
137|`/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers/provision-workspace-subscriber`; scripts
138|are packaged without their source `.sh` suffix and resolve their companion
139|entry points in the same directory.
140|
141|`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` declares the exact source, destination
142|basename and mode in `RELEASE_HELPER_INPUTS`:
143|
144|| Source under `deploy/` | Packaged helpers/assets |
145|| --- | --- |
146|| `scripts/*.sh` (explicit names only) | `provision-workspace-subscriber`, `prepare-instance-disk`, `sync-instance-upgrade`, `prepare-chatbot-adoption`, `bind-instance-root`, `3tchedfs-invoke` |
147|| `runit/libexec-3tched/` (explicit provisioning dependencies) | `op-identity-root`, `op-identity-image`, `attach-host-workspace-folders`, `restore-chatbot-root` |
148|| `workspace-image/` (offline image inputs) | `prepare-lungs-client` from `prepare-lungs-client.sh`, `3tchedfs-mount-preflight`, `mount.fuse.3tchedFS`, `3tchedfs.service`, `3tchedfs.fstab`, `3tched-lungs.conf` |
149|
150|Executables use mode 0755; the guest service, fstab fragment and tmpfiles
151|configuration use mode 0644. Preparation requires every declared source to
152|be a readable regular non-symlink file; destination modes come from the
153|declaration, not the checkout's executable bits.
154|It copies bytes only; none of these helpers is invoked by golden preparation.
155|The existing application helpers, including the separate host
156|`mount-3tchedfs` adapter, remain included. The guest `mount.fuse.3tchedFS`
157|asset is not installed over the host's mount adapter.
158|
159|The dependency split is deliberate:
160|
161|- The provisioner delegates disk, upgrade, binding and adoption steps to its
162|  packaged siblings. Its legacy physical-seed path also uses
163|  `op-identity-root` and `attach-host-workspace-folders`; the root helper uses
164|  `op-identity-image` to verify seed metadata. GPT boot restoration uses
165|  `restore-chatbot-root` and `sync-instance-upgrade`.
166|- Mounted calls use the activated `/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs`
167|  and caller-bound `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`. Packing the client/wrapper grants
168|  no authority and does not make an unprovisioned identity callable.
169|- `prepare-lungs-client` consumes its adjacent guest assets plus a separately
170|  selected immutable release's client and public catalog. These are image
171|  preparation inputs, not a root image, private state or an instruction to
172|  modify a seed with retained leaves. Guest paths stay distinct from host
173|  paths; packaging does not mount, format, provision, adopt or start a guest.
174|- `identity-roots`, Incus, host network/storage services and the independent
175|  release bootstrap remain base prerequisites. Their service definitions are
176|  not made application-owned merely because a helper is packaged. The
177|  existing enabled/retired plus `# op-dbus-release: application` gate still
178|  selects application runit definitions. No base helper installation, boot
179|  wiring, grants, credentials or storage receipts are rewritten here.
180|
181|The historical `op-identity-lungs-hook` is not selected for new provisioning,
182|and `op-lungs-check` still uses the retired sibling receipt protocol; neither
183|is restored to the payload. Existing host hook bindings are not rewritten or
184|deleted by preparation.
185|
186|**Caller integration is separate from inclusion.** Defaults in the
187|provisioner/root helper and the base `restore-chatbot-root` caller must select
188|the reviewed helpers at the intended ownership boundary; an old
189|`/usr/local/libexec/3tched/...` call does not use these newly packaged bytes.
190|Do not repoint all base services or replace that entire host directory.
191|`prepare-lungs-client` also still requires reconciliation of its historical
192|`/opt/op-dbus/releases/*` input guard and `var/lib/opdbus/plugin-blobs`
193|catalog suffix with the native slot contract and the prepared
194|`usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs` catalog before using it on a native release.
195|
196|The prepared-source inventory hashes these files under the existing helper
197|target; no new release target or deployment path is introduced. Its shell
198|scanner examines helper scripts, but restart consumers are derived from
199|release-owned runit services, not from operator CLI availability. In
200|`crates/op-cozo-store/src/bin/inventory/mod.rs`, `declared_paths` does not
201|resolve `realpath -e`/`${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` sibling selection or caller-selected
202|image roots, and `collect_consumers` checks dependency blockers only when
203|reachable from an application service. It does not establish standalone
204|provisioner completeness. Guest `/usr/share/op-dbus/lungs-*` references also
205|belong to the image, not missing host payload. Inventory work must distinguish
206|those scopes without suppressing unknown executable/configuration errors or
207|inventing application consumers. Do not add base-service application markers
208|to make preparation pass. Require the actual prepared graph and native
209|activation receipt before claiming delivery. This source packaging change
210|alone proves neither graph generation nor provisioning/boot readiness;
211|deployment remains
212|`./activate-golden.sh` and its existing snapshot/send-receive controller.
213|
214|### Separate host filesystem surfaces
215|
216|Our filesystem executable is `3tched-fs` (Cargo package `tched-fs`, retained
217|source directory `crates/threetched-fs`). Its plugin is `tched_fs`, displayed
218|as 3tchedFS. The external ZeroClaw-derived executable remains `threetched`.
219|The host projects two disjoint views of the same sealed catalog:
220|
221|| Mount | Projected plugins |
222|| --- | --- |
223|| `/run/mounts/3tchedFS` | OP-DBUS plugins, including `tched_fs`, excluding the two below |
224|| `/run/mounts/threetched` | `threetched`, `tched_router` |
225|
226|This is the consolidation source selection. The retired `tched_plugins` and
227|`tched_skills` wrappers must be absent from the matching freshly sealed release
228|catalog before activation. Existing live mounts are not changed by these source
229|edits; record their catalog and readiness receipts separately.
230|
231|Both use our FUSE engine and kernel subtype `fuse.3tchedFS`; their kernel
232|source labels distinguish `3tchedFS` and `threetched`. Filtering changes only
233|the view: the catalog pin, per-plugin schema hashes and operation admission
234|remain authoritative. A mounted schema does not prove session provisioning
235|or permission to execute an operation.
236|
237|`deploy/host-fuse/3tchedfs.fstab` declares the two mounts. The release carries
238|`mount-3tchedfs` under `/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers`; the host's
239|`/usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS` and `/etc/rcS.d/S13op-3tchedfs-mount` link to
240|that adapter. Explicit late mounting after `S12op-release-activate` is why
241|the entries use `noauto`. The old `threetched-fs` runit service is retired.
242|The adapter uses the existing root-owned mode-0400 or mode-0600
243|`/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session` and `human-lungs-call-owner-uid` selection
244|files; it never mints an identity or grants access.
245|
246|After a catalog-changing activation, unmount the old host views normally,
247|then mount each declared fstab target to capture the new release's catalog.
248|Preserve any outstanding operation receipts before unmounting. Boot wiring
249|and live mount readiness are separate from a reboot verification.
250|The host's fstab entries and helper/boot symlinks live outside the application
251|snapshot. Rolling back to a release that predates the two-view adapter also
252|requires restoring the saved host mount configuration; application rollback
253|does not undo those host files.
254|
255|After extracting deterministic UI assets into the prepared tree, set
256|`dashboard/index.html` to the preparation timestamp before taking the read-only

553|## Coding retrieval deadlines
554|
555|Coding retrieval has one total budget covering embedding and collection
556|queries. Defaults are 5 seconds for completion, 10 seconds for search, and
557|30 seconds for deep retrieval. Operators may set
558|`COGNITIVE_MCP_RETRIEVAL_DEADLINE_MS`, or override a mode with
559|`COGNITIVE_MCP_COMPLETION_DEADLINE_MS`, `COGNITIVE_MCP_SEARCH_DEADLINE_MS`,
560|or `COGNITIVE_MCP_DEEP_DEADLINE_MS`. Values are bounded to 100–120,000 ms.
561|Search reports failure when its budget expires; context returns an explicit

563|also reports an error. Partial results remain available when at least one
564|collection query succeeds.

304|#### Branch F — /dev/fuse 设备权限问题
305|
306|**触发条件**：容器或非 root 用户启动 FUSE daemon 时出现 Permission denied。
307|
308|```
309|L2 诊断：
310|├── 1. ls -la /dev/fuse（设备节点权限）
311|├── 2. getfacl /dev/fuse（ACL 权限检查）
312|├── 3. cat /proc/<daemon_pid>/status | grep Cap（daemon 能力集）
313|├── 4. grep fuse /etc/group（fuse 用户组）
314|├── 5. groups <daemon_user>（用户所属组）
315|├── 6. cat /etc/fuse.conf（FUSE 全局配置）
316|├── 7. capsh --print | grep fuse（进程能力检查）
317|├── 8. container environment: cat /proc/1/cgroup（容器内 cgroup 检查）
318|│
319|└── L3 根因判定：
320|    ├── /dev/fuse 权限 0600 root:root → 非 root 用户无法访问
321|    ├── daemon 用户不在 fuse 组 → 缺少 /dev/fuse 访问权限
322|    ├── 容器内未挂载 /dev/fuse → 设备节点不存在
323|    ├── 容器缺少 CAP_SYS_ADMIN 或 CAP_MKNOD → 无法操作 FUSE 设备
324|    ├── user_allow_other 未在 /etc/fuse.conf 启用 → 无法使用 allow_other
325|    ├── AppArmor/SELinux 阻止 FUSE 操作 → 安全策略限制
326|    └── daemon 进程 capabilities 被移除 → container runtime 降权
327|```
328|
329|**典型输出**：
330|```
331|结论: /dev/fuse 权限 0600 root:root，daemon 以非 root 用户
332|      运行且不在 fuse 用户组中。
333|      daemon 启动日志显示 "Permission denied" 打开 /dev/fuse。
334|根因: /dev/fuse 设备节点仅 root 可读写，FUSE daemon
335|      以普通用户运行且未加入 fuse 组，无法打开设备。
336|```

339|
340|**触发条件**：内核 Panic、Oops、soft lockup 与 FUSE 相关，或已知 FUSE 内核 Bug。
341|
342|```
343|L2 诊断：
344|├── 1. dmesg | grep -iE "fuse|libfuse"（内核 FUSE 消息）
345|├── 2. dmesg | grep -iE "kernel panic|Oops|BUG|soft lockup"（内核异常）

348|├── 5. cat /proc/self/mounts | grep fuse（所有 FUSE 挂载）
349|├── 6. cat /sys/fs/fuse/connections/*/abort（abort 状态）
350|├── 7. test -f /var/crash/vmcore* 2>/dev/null && ls -lh /var/crash/（crash dump 检查）
351|├── 8. grep -i fuse /var/log/messages | tail -20（系统日志）
352|│
353|└── L3 根因判定：
354|    ├── 已知 FUSE 内核 Bug 列表匹配（CVE-xxxx-xxxx / 内核 commit）
355|    ├── 特定内核版本 + FUSE 版本组合已知不兼容
356|    ├── CR2 地址在 FUSE 模块区域内 → FUSE 内核模块导致 Panic
357|    ├── soft lockup 栈显示在 fuse_* 函数中 → FUSE 内核路径问题
358|    ├── 大规模并发操作触发的竞态条件 → 内核 FUSE 并发 Bug
359|    └── FUSE 模块参数不合理导致内核异常 → max_read 过小/过大
360|```
361|
362|**典型输出**：
363|```
364|结论: dmesg 显示 "kernel BUG at fs/fuse/dev.c:1234"，
365|      内核版本 5.15.0-rc3 存在已知 FUSE 并发访问 Bug。
366|      CR2 地址 0xffff888123456789 在 fuse_dev_do_write 函数范围内。
367|根因: 内核 FUSE 模块在特定内核版本下存在并发竞态条件，
368|      多线程并发写操作触发内核 BUG。
369|```
370|
371|#### Branch H — 混合/复杂 FUSE 故障
372|
373|**触发条件**：多种现象共存，或以上分支无法覆盖的复杂 FUSE 问题。
374|
375|```
376|L2 诊断：
377|├── 1. 执行所有以上分支的 L2 诊断（汇总所有证据）
378|├── 2. 交叉对比各分支症状（判定主次故障）
379|├── 3. 完整 strace -f -e trace=all -p <daemon_pid> -o /tmp/strace.log
380|├── 4. lsof -p <daemon_pid>（daemon 打开的文件/连接）
381|├── 5. tcpdump -i any host <backend_storage_ip>（后端存储网络抓包）
382|├── 6. strace -e trace=all ls -la <mount_point> 2>&1（客户端操作全追踪）
383|├── 7. 对比故障前后的 FUSE 配置快照（连接数、参数、daemon 版本）
384|│
385|└── L3 根因判定：
386|    ├── 按故障链优先级排序（先解决依赖的下层问题）
387|    ├── 多故障串联（daemon 崩溃 → 残留连接 → 新 daemon 无法挂载）
388|    ├── 配置错误叠加（max_read 过小 + 线程池太小 + writeback 未启用）
389|    ├── 环境变化触发（内核升级、cgroup 限制、SELinux 策略变更）
390|    └── 复杂的 libfuse API 使用错误（回调注册、会话管理、信号处理）
391|```
392|
393|**典型输出**：
394|```
395|结论: 多种故障共存：daemon 线程池过小（4 线程）导致写性能差，
396|      同时 max_read=4K 进一步退化读性能，writeback cache 启用
397|      但 daemon 未正确处理 ->write 回调。
398|根因: 多重配置叠加导致 FUSE 极端性能退化，建议逐一修复：
399|      1. 增大线程池至 16+
400|      2. 设置 max_read=128K+

2|name: ovs-db-analysis
3|description: >-
4|  Analyze Open vSwitch data from sosreport — conf.db, OpenFlow dumps, port stats,
5|  tunnels, and datapath health. Use when troubleshooting OVS packet drops, flow
6|  performance, bridge/port/interface issues, DPDK vs kernel datapath, or when the
7|  user mentions sosreport openvswitch, ovs-ofctl, ovsdb-tool, or ovs-db-analysis.
8|---
9|
10|# OVS Database and Flow Analysis
11|
12|This skill provides detailed analysis of Open vSwitch (OVS) data collected via sosreport. It operates in four modes:
13|
14|1. **Default mode**: Full analysis - conf.db + all text files (requires ovsdb-tool, falls back to text files if not available)
15|2. **Database mode (`--db`)**: Database only - analyze conf.db (requires ovsdb-tool)
16|3. **Text files mode (`--flows-only`)**: Text files only - no ovsdb-tool needed
17|4. **Query mode (`--query`)**: Run custom OVSDB JSON queries (requires ovsdb-tool)
18|
19|## When to Use This Skill
20|
21|Use this skill when:
22|- **Troubleshooting packet drops** - Find drop flows being hit
23|- **Analyzing flow performance** - View top flows by packet count
24|- Analyzing OVS configuration from a sosreport
25|- Troubleshooting bridge, port, or interface issues
26|- Investigating DPDK vs kernelspace datapath
27|- Reviewing tunnel configurations (VXLAN, Geneve, GRE)
28|- Checking port statistics (drops, errors, traffic)
29|- Mapping Kubernetes pods to OVS interfaces
30|
31|## Prerequisites
32|
33|**Default mode** (full analysis):
34|- **ovsdb-tool** must be installed (from openvswitch package)
35|- Falls back to `--flows-only` if ovsdb-tool not found
36|- Sosreport with `sos_commands/openvswitch/` directory and `conf.db`
37|
38|**Database mode** (`--db`):
39|- **ovsdb-tool** must be installed (from openvswitch package)
40|  - Check: `which ovsdb-tool`
41|  - Fedora/RHEL: `sudo dnf install openvswitch`
42|  - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install openvswitch-common`
43|- Sosreport with `conf.db` file
44|
45|**Text files mode** (`--flows-only`):
46|- No special tools needed - works out of the box!
47|- Sosreport with `sos_commands/openvswitch/` directory
48|
49|**Query mode** (`--query`):
50|- **ovsdb-tool** must be installed
51|- Incompatible with `--flows-only`
52|
53|## File Locations in Sosreport
54|
55|The sosreport collects:
56|```
57|sosreport-hostname-date/
58|├── etc/openvswitch/conf.db              (OVS database - for --db mode)
59|├── var/lib/openvswitch/conf.db          (alternate location)
60|└── sos_commands/openvswitch/            (default mode uses these)
61|    ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_show              (topology)
62|    ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_bridge       (bridge details)
63|    ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_interface    (interface details)
64|    ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_Open_vSwitch (system info)
65|    ├── ovs-ofctl_dump-flows_<bridge>    (OpenFlow entries)
66|    ├── ovs-ofctl_dump-ports_<bridge>    (Port statistics)
67|    ├── ovs-appctl_coverage.show         (internal stats)
68|    ├── ovs-appctl_upcall.show           (datapath health)
69|    ├── ovs-appctl_tnl.ports.show_-v     (tunnel ports)
70|    └── ...
71|```
72|
73|## Analysis Script
74|
75|The analysis script is located at:
76|```
77|<plugin-root>/skills/ovs-db-analysis/scripts/analyze_ovs_db.py
78|```
79|
80|## Implementation Steps
81|
82|### Step 1: Locate the Analysis Script
83|
84|```bash
85|SCRIPT_PATH=$(find ~ -name "analyze_ovs_db.py" -path "*/sosreport/skills/ovs-db-analysis/scripts/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
86|
87|if [ -z "$SCRIPT_PATH" ]; then
88|    echo "ERROR: analyze_ovs_db.py script not found."
89|    exit 1
90|fi
91|```
92|
93|### Step 2: Run the Analysis
94|
95|```bash
96|# Default: Full analysis - conf.db + text files (requires ovsdb-tool)
97|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport-hostname-date/
98|
99|# Analyze from archive
100|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport-hostname-date.tar.xz
101|
102|# Database only mode (requires ovsdb-tool)
103|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --db
104|
105|# Text files only mode (no ovsdb-tool needed)
106|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --flows-only
107|```
108|
109|### Step 3: Custom Queries (Optional, requires --db)
110|
111|For specific investigations, use raw OVSDB queries:
112|
113|```bash
114|# Query all bridges
115|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Bridge", "where":[], "columns":["name","datapath_type","fail_mode"]}]'
116|
117|# Query VXLAN interfaces
118|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Interface", "where":[["type","==","vxlan"]], "columns":["name","options"]}]'
119|
120|# Query interfaces with errors
121|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Interface", "where":[], "columns":["name","error"]}]'
122|```
123|
124|## Analysis Output
125|
126|The default mode analyzes:
127|
128|| Analysis | Source File | Description |
129||----------|-------------|-------------|
130|| System Info | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_Open_vSwitch` | OVS/DPDK version, system type, external IDs |
131|| Topology | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_show` | Bridge overview with ports grouped by type |
132|| Bridge Details | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_bridge` | Datapath type, fail mode, CT zones |
133|| Interfaces | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_interface` | By type, pod interfaces with mapping |
134|| OpenFlow | `ovs-ofctl_dump-flows_*` | Flow counts, drops, top flows |
135|| Port Stats | `ovs-ofctl_dump-ports_*` | RX/TX drops and errors |
136|| Tunnels | `ovs-appctl_tnl.ports.show_-v` | Configured tunnel ports |
137|| Datapath Health | `ovs-appctl_upcall.show` | Flow table usage vs limit |
138|| OVS Stats | `ovs-appctl_coverage.show` | Internal counters (netlink, OVSDB, etc.) |
139|
140|## OpenFlow Analysis Features
141|
142|| Feature | Description |
143||---------|-------------|
144|| Flow Count | Total flows per bridge (total, drop, with hits) |
145|| Drop Detection | Flows with `actions=drop` that have packet hits |
146|| Top Flows | Most active flows sorted by n_packets |
147|| Table Distribution | Flow counts per OpenFlow table |
148|| Port Drops | RX/TX drop counters per port |
149|| Port Errors | RX/TX error counters per port |
150|| Datapath Health | Flow table usage vs limit (from upcall.show) |
151|| OVS Stats | Internal statistics (netlink, OpenFlow, OVSDB transactions) |
152|
153|## OVN Internal Tables (Ignore Drops in These)
154|
155|When analyzing drop flows in OVN-managed bridges (br-int), **ignore drops in table 44 and tables 64-87** as these are internal OVN mechanics, not security policy or real packet drops.
156|
157|> **⚠️ Note:** OVN and OVS are complex systems and table mappings can change between releases. Always verify drop analysis against the specific OVN version in use. When in doubt, check the OVN source code for your release.
158|
159|| Table | Name | Purpose |
160||-------|------|---------|
161|| **44** | **CHK_LB_OUTPUT** | **Loopback prevention - drops packets that would loop back (high volume, normal)** |
162|| 64 | SAVE_INPORT | Save ingress port for later |
163|| 65 | LOG_TO_PHY | Logical to physical mapping |
164|| 66 | MAC_BINDING | MAC binding lookups |
165|| 67 | MAC_LOOKUP | MAC address table lookups |
166|| 68-69 | CHK_LB_HAIRPIN | Load balancer hairpin checks |
167|| 70 | CT_SNAT_HAIRPIN | Conntrack SNAT hairpin |
168|| 71-72 | GET/LOOKUP_FDB | FDB (forwarding DB) lookups |
169|| 73-74 | CHK_IN_PORT_SEC | Ingress port security |
170|| 75 | CHK_OUT_PORT_SEC | Egress port security |
171|| 76-77 | ECMP_NH | ECMP next-hop handling |
172|| 78 | CHK_LB_AFFINITY | Load balancer affinity |
173|| **79** | **MAC_CACHE_USE** | **MAC cache miss (high volume, normal)** |
174|| 80 | CT_ZONE_LOOKUP | Conntrack zone lookup |
175|| 81-83 | CT_ORIG_*_LOAD | Conntrack original tuple loading |
176|| 84 | FLOOD_REMOTE_CHASSIS | Remote chassis flooding |
177|| 85 | CT_STATE_SAVE | Conntrack state save |
178|| 86 | CT_ORIG_PROTO_LOAD | Conntrack protocol loading |
179|| 87 | GET_REMOTE_FDB | Remote FDB lookup |
180|
181|**Relevant drop tables for troubleshooting:**
182|- **Table 9**: Ingress ACLs - actual policy drops (look for `reg0=0x8000`)
183|- **Table 0**: Initial classification drops
184|- **Tables < 64**: Generally meaningful drops
185|
186|## Common Analysis Scenarios
187|
188|### 1. Troubleshooting Packet Drops
189|
190|```bash
191|# Quick analysis (default mode, no ovsdb-tool)
192|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/
193|```
194|
195|Look for:
196|- **ACTIVE DROP FLOWS** section showing flows dropping packets
197|- **PORT STATISTICS** showing ports with drops/errors
198|
199|### 2. Checking DPDK Configuration
200|
201|```bash
202|# Default mode shows DPDK info from text files
203|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/
204|
205|# Or use database mode for custom queries
206|python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Open_vSwitch", "where":[], "columns":["dpdk_initialized","other_config"]}]'
207|```
208|
209|### 3. Investigating Pod Connectivity
210|
211|The interface analysis shows pod-to-OVS mapping:
212|- Interfaces with `external_ids` containing `iface-id`
213|- Interface names ending with `_h` (veth host side)
214|
215|### 4. Datapath Health Check
216|
217|The upcall stats show:
218|```
219|DATAPATH FLOW TABLE HEALTH
220|  Current flows: 155 / 200,000 (0.1% used)
221|  Average: 156, Max seen: 215
222|  ✓ Flow table healthy
223|```
224|
225|If usage > 90%, flows are being evicted too aggressively.

3|#
4|#   sudo ./activate-golden.sh

6|# Run it after the release build and seal:
7|#   CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
8|#   sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm && sudo target/release/opblob persist
9|# OP_RELEASE_DIR selects one prepared optimized artifact directory for both
10|# release-controller verification and golden preparation (default target/release).
11|#
12|# What it does:
13|# 1. Native provision-slots reconciles any interrupted transaction and prepares
14|#    the owned golden/slot layout. Recovery-only work stops this invocation.
15|# 2. Prepares /opt/op-dbus/golden from target/release and the sealed catalog
16|#    (internal helper deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh; it never builds or seals).
17|# 3. Native release sends/receives the immutable generation into the inactive
18|#    slot, rotates read-only overlays at the inventory's owned host targets,
19|#    and restores affected consumers' wanted states. Only active + previous remain.
20|#
21|# Undo the last release:
22|#   sudo /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch rollback
23|set -eu
24|PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
25|LC_ALL=C
26|export PATH LC_ALL
27|
28|REPO=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
29|OP_RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$REPO/target/release"}")
30|export OP_RELEASE_DIR
31|RELEASE_BASE=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
32|RELEASE_LAUNCH=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release-launch
33|RELEASE_BIN=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release
34|RELEASE_BOOT=/etc/init.d/op-release-activate

36|[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: run as root (sudo ./activate-golden.sh)' >&2; exit 1; }
37|[ "$#" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: takes no arguments' >&2; exit 1; }
38|# Check the execution path before invoking any installed kit code. The launcher

43|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] &&

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|# Installed base-system launcher; holds one open-file-description lock through exec.
3|# Base-installation authorization contract (never installed by this launcher):
4|# /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release is root:root 0755, outside every application
5|# overlay, containing ONLY op-release, op-release-launch and manifest.sha256.
6|# The executables and /etc/init.d/op-release-activate are root:root 0755 regular
7|# single-link files. The manifest is root:root 0600, with exactly one canonical
8|# SHA256 line ("<64 lowercase hex>  <absolute path>") for each of those THREE
9|# executables, including the init script outside this directory. No self-entry.
10|# Authorize those bytes together from the independently authored op-deployment
11|# op-release build and these two source scripts; never approve a historical
12|# controller by copying or renaming it. Publish the manifest only after review
13|# of the complete installed set, with release/boot callers inactive during the
14|# base installation. This is root approval, not a remotely signed provenance
15|# claim. No generated manifest, fallback, or live installation is performed here.
16|# Existing receiver.json, first-activation.json and native lifetime gates remain
17|# separate authorities; this kit neither creates nor relaxes them.
18|set -eu
19|PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
20|LC_ALL=C
21|export PATH LC_ALL
22|umask 077
23|base=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
24|state=/var/lib/opdbus-release
25|runtime=/run/opdbus-release
26|[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo 'usage: op-release-launch {release|deploy|provision-slots|status|activate a|b|rollback|abort|boot}' >&2; exit 2; }
27|verb=$1
28|case "$verb" in
29|  activate) [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && { [ "$2" = a ] || [ "$2" = b ]; } || exit 2 ;;
30|  release|deploy|provision-slots|status|rollback|abort|boot) [ "$#" -eq 1 ] || exit 2 ;;
31|  *) echo 'unsupported release verb; host/Incus provisioning belongs to its existing owner' >&2; exit 2 ;;
32|esac
33|# Independently authored, read-only release-kit verifier. It intentionally has
34|# no shell-source dependency and knows no storage daemon, guard tool or helper.
35|fail() { printf 'op-release-launch: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
36|secure_directory() {
37|    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] &&
38|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$1")" = 0:0 ] &&
39|        [ "$((0$(stat -c %a "$1") & 07022))" -eq 0 ] ||
40|        fail "insecure directory: $1"
41|}
42|secure_file() {
43|    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] &&
44|        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a:%h "$1")" = "0:0:$2:1" ] ||
45|        fail "expected root-owned, non-symlink, single-link mode $2 file: $1"
46|}
47|verify_release_kit() {
48|    for directory in / /usr /usr/local /usr/local/libexec "$base" /etc /etc/init.d; do
49|        secure_directory "$directory"
50|    done
51|    [ "$(stat -c %a "$base")" = 755 ] || fail 'release-kit directory must be mode 0755'
52|    secure_file "$base/op-release" 755
53|    secure_file "$base/op-release-launch" 755
54|    secure_file /etc/init.d/op-release-activate 755
55|    secure_file "$base/manifest.sha256" 600
56|    # Reject mixed kits, including unmanifested hidden files and subdirectories.
57|    for entry in "$base"/* "$base"/.[!.]* "$base"/..?*; do
58|        [ -e "$entry" ] || [ -L "$entry" ] || continue
59|        case "${entry##*/}" in
60|            op-release|op-release-launch|manifest.sha256) ;;
61|            *) fail "unexpected release-kit entry: $entry" ;;
62|        esac
63|    done
64|    [ "$(stat -c %s "$base/manifest.sha256")" -le 1024 ] ||
65|        fail 'release-kit manifest is oversized'
66|    awk '
67|        BEGIN {
68|            allowed["/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release"] = 1
69|            allowed["/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch"] = 1
70|            allowed["/etc/init.d/op-release-activate"] = 1
71|        }
72|        {
73|            if (NF != 2 || length($1) != 64 || $1 ~ /[^0-9a-f]/ ||
74|                $0 != $1 "  " $2 || !($2 in allowed) || seen[$2]++) {
75|                invalid = 1
76|                exit 1
77|            }
78|            count++
79|        }
80|        END { if (invalid || count != 3) exit 1 }
81|    ' "$base/manifest.sha256" || fail 'manifest must name exactly the three approved release-kit files'
82|    sha256sum --strict --check --quiet "$base/manifest.sha256" ||
83|        fail 'approved release-kit digest mismatch'
84|    # Existing approval policy data only. New kernels/BTF require separate
85|    # review; successful hashing or a lifetime feature does not confer approval.
86|    btf=$(sha256sum /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux) || fail 'kernel BTF is unavailable'
87|    kernel=$(uname -r) || fail 'kernel release is unavailable'
88|    case "$kernel ${btf%% *}" in
89|        '6.18.57-x64v3-op-release-lifetime1-xanmod1 418e74eb9598f5747b4039d3934d77f244b1d9e7ba0f64d729c21a6ddebdb975' | \
90|        '6.18.56-x64v3-xanmod1 488c010609b5e98244ddf062cd7bcaf86b17b2a32bc70b369ca3c2a4efd59cb2' | \
91|        '6.12.111+deb13-amd64 117c3da349bc97db5eb4c0627b7b12afc9a3f83686e35c2b28d6031e13767018') ;;
92|        *) fail 'kernel/BTF pair requires separate policy approval' ;;
93|    esac
94|}
95|verify_release_kit
96|if [ "$verb" = status ]; then
97|    exec "$base/op-release" "$@"
98|fi
99|[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo 'release requires the authorized root owner' >&2; exit 1; }
100|for directory in /var /var/lib "$state" /run; do
101|    secure_directory "$directory"
102|done
103|secure_file "$state/lock" 600
104|if [ -e "$runtime" ] || [ -L "$runtime" ]; then secure_directory "$runtime"; fi
105|install -d -m 0755 -o root -g root "$runtime"
106|exec 9>>"$state/lock"
107|if ! flock -n 9; then
108|    if [ "$verb" = boot ]; then
109|        temporary=$(mktemp "$runtime/.ready.XXXXXX")
110|        printf 'recovery-pending lock-busy\n' > "$temporary"
111|        chmod 0644 "$temporary"
112|        mv -f "$temporary" "$runtime/ready"
113|    fi
114|    echo 'another release transaction holds fd9' >&2
115|    exit 1
116|fi
117|if [ "$verb" != boot ]; then
118|    # Membership is preinstalled authority, not a request to turn the guard on.
119|    # Never create a cgroup, alter trusted maps, auto-rearm or require guard ON.
120|    [ -f /sys/fs/cgroup/opdbus-release/cgroup.procs ] || {
121|        echo 'approved existing release cgroup is absent' >&2; exit 1;
122|    }
123|    printf '%s\n' "$$" > /sys/fs/cgroup/opdbus-release/cgroup.procs
124|fi
125|# No top-level mount, independent recovery process, or restart-all loop here.
126|exec "$base/op-release" "$@"","total_lines":126,"file_size":6169,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|### BEGIN INIT INFO
3|# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
4|# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
5|# Required-Stop:
6|# Default-Start:     S
7|# Default-Stop:
8|# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
9|### END INIT INFO
10|# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
11|# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
12|# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
13|set -eu
14|PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
15|export PATH
16|fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
17|case "${1:-}" in
18|    start)
19|        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
20|        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
21|        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
22|        ;;
23|    stop) exit 0 ;;
24|esac
25|[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
26|[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
27|    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
28|fs_name=$1
29|mount_path=$2
30|case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
31|    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
32|    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
33|    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
34|esac
35|upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router
36|catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
37|options=$4
38|while [ -n "$options" ]; do
39|    option=${options%%,*}
40|    case "$option" in
41|        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
42|        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
43|    esac
44|    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
45|done
46|protected_file() {
47|    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
48|    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
49|}
50|session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
51|owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
52|protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
53|session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
54|printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
55|owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
56|case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
57|[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
58|ensure_dir() {
59|    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
60|    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
61|        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
62|}
63|ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
64|ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
65|runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
66|ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
67|umask 077
68|exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
69|flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
70|mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
71|ready() {
72|    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
73|    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
74|    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
75|        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
76|        .mount_identity.session == $session and
77|        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
78|    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
79|    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
80|        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
81|        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
82|        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
83|        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
84|         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
85|        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
86|        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
87|            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
88|        end)
89|    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
90|}
91|if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
92|    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
93|    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
94|    exit 0
95|fi
96|binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
97|store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
98|[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
99|case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
100|    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
101|esac
102|[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
103|ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
104|ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
105|[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
106|ensure_dir "$store" 700
107|# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
108|# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
109|"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
110|    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
111|nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
112|    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
113|    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
114|    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
115|    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
116|    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
117|daemon_pid=$!
118|printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
119|attempt=0
120|while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
121|    if ready; then
122|        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
123|        exit 0
124|    fi
125|    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
126|    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
127|    sleep 0.1
128|done
129|kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
130|wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
131|fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"","total_lines":131,"file_size":5668,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}

{"content":"1|//! Adapter for the pinned downstream Btrfs quiescent-destroy ABI.
2|//! No userspace scan, kernel-version guess, or ordinary-delete fallback is safe.
3|use std::{io, os::fd::{AsRawFd, BorrowedFd}};
4|use uuid::Uuid;
5|
6|// deploy/release/lifetime/0001-btrfs-quiescent-destroy.patch, native Linux ABI:
7|// _IOW(BTRFS_IOCTL_MAGIC /* 0x94 */, 255, struct ... /* 96 bytes */).
8|const SNAP_DESTROY_QUIESCENT: libc::c_ulong = 0x4060_94ff;
9|
10|#[repr(C)]
11|struct QuiescentDestroy {
12|    subvolid: u64,
13|    fsid: [u8; 16],
14|    uuid: [u8; 16],
15|    received_uuid: [u8; 16],
16|    flags: u64,
17|    reserved: [u64; 4],
18|}
19|const _: () = assert!(std::mem::size_of::<QuiescentDestroy>() == 96);
20|
21|// The caller journals exact identity before this call and must close its own
22|// target-root descriptors/mounts first. `top` is a different root on the same
23|// filesystem. Source snapshots and aborted incoming roots use this same path;
24|// they must be read-only too (a zero received UUID is valid).
25|//
26|// The kernel holds admission closed continuously from its reference census
27|// through unlink. Success permanently closes the old incarnation; no userspace
28|// lease/Drop unlock is needed while the caller waits for the cleaner and renames
29|// the incoming root. Live-alias rejection precedes root unlink. Other failures
30|// can follow unlink, so recovery must reconcile identity after every error.
31|// The ABI reserves EBUSY/ESTALE/EROFS/EINVAL for pre-unlink rejection and maps
32|// all failures after root unlink starts to EIO. EIO never promises rollback.
33|// ENOENT is special to this checked ABI: its kernel lifetime registry includes
34|// orphan root objects through final free and proves the exact generation has
35|// no live inode aliases. Pathname absence or native cleaner completion alone
36|// never substitutes for that proof. A busy orphan remains admission-closed.
37|// ENOTTY means the required kernel is absent and must remain a hard failure.
38|pub fn destroy(
39|    top: BorrowedFd<'_>,
40|    fsid: Uuid,
41|    subvolid: u64,
42|    native_uuid: Uuid,
43|    received_uuid: Uuid,
44|) -> io::Result<()> {
45|    let args = QuiescentDestroy {
46|        subvolid,
47|        fsid: fsid.into_bytes(),
48|        uuid: native_uuid.into_bytes(),
49|        received_uuid: received_uuid.into_bytes(),
50|        flags: 0,
51|        reserved: [0; 4],
52|    };
53|    // SAFETY: the fixed-layout, fully initialized 96-byte input and borrowed
54|    // ioctl-capable directory descriptor remain valid throughout the syscall.
55|    let result = unsafe { libc::ioctl(top.as_raw_fd(), SNAP_DESTROY_QUIESCENT, &args) };
56|    match result {
57|        0 => Ok(()),
58|        -1 => Err(io::Error::last_os_error()),
59|        _ => Err(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::EPROTO)),
60|    }
61|}","total_lines":61,"file_size":2684,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}
